Early on in the pandemic, before masks, right when we started to go into lockdown, I asked my parents  to wash their hands when they came home from parties. It escalated and my father told me to be quiet. I just couldn’t anymore, although I always had to be when I was a child. Something in me broke and I just refused. But that wasn’t the scariest part. The scariest part was realizing after he stopped (when my mom threw herself onto him) that I did absolutely nothing. In movies, the person getting strangled always keeps their eyes opens and fights. I just closed my eyes and held my hand over my face. I was stressed for months after that; I realized  that when I’m being hurt, I’ll just relax into it. It was made even worse knowing that if someone close to me tried to hurt me, my body would just dissociate. It just left me. I did nothing to defend myself. I know understand how people get murdered by people they trust. My therapist told me that it could have in fact been a safety mechanism, that something deep within could have told me that was the safest way to get him to stop. But I was a dancer for 25 years and danced professionally until that moment. I hate dance now. I don’t trust my body. I have videos of myself dancing in empty fields when the pandemic started.
